chd.label: Campaign history 2017-2026
chd.portal: KP+TD UC spotting workbook (Dropbox, shared by EOC data cell)
chd.note: 134MB workbook; first read streams the DATA sheet into cache/ch_rows.pkl (~3 min), later runs reuse the cache until the workbook mtime changes.

can.label: Campaign analysis - district x campaign template rows
can.portal: KP+TD UC spotting workbook (Dropbox, shared by EOC data cell)
can.note: District-level aggregate of the same DATA sheet as chd: recorded missed NA/refusal, same-day covered, ICM missed + reasons and recall check/verified, market survey, LQAS pass/intermediate/fail, PCM clusters/checks/FM per campaign per district. Campaign order asserted against CHD.

snd.label: Upcoming campaign scope + day-wise targets
snd.portal: Final scope workbook issued for the upcoming campaign (D:\AMAZON DATA\SNID <campaign> folder)
snd.note: When a new campaign scope arrives, edit config.name and config.start here - the tab title, hero chip, countdown popup and Evening Review day dates all follow SND.n / SND.st. Rename the tab labels separately (search the old campaign name across the 4 variants).

ucc.label: UC criteria (EOC master categorization: Afghan bordering / core / endemic / high risk / rest of KP)
ucc.portal: EOC UC master categorization workbook (Master Sheet tab) - IDIMS + COMNet + EOC Cat blocks
ucc.note: One row per UC (1,402) with the EOC categorization blocks. Only the geo columns plus `Boardering UC` and `SKP/Rest KP` are read; COMNet staff names, PDA and IDIMS figures stay out of the payload. District categories are NOT taken from the workbook - they come from the dashboard's own `const SND` (the upcoming round's scope categories), so the criteria vocabulary follows the campaign. A UC flagged as bordering Afghanistan is labelled `Afghan bordering` even when its district sits in another category (8 UCs of KHYBER, 3 of WAZIR-N, 4 of WAZIR-S Lower). Districts outside the SND scope fall back to `Rest of KP`, asserted against the master's own SKP/Rest KP value. `al` carries legacy district spellings used by older payloads (combined WAZIR-S in CHD). Drop a newer Master Sheet into Downloads and run `--only ucc --force`. `aluc` repeats those Afghan-bordering UC names under legacy district names (config `legacy_afg`, incl. CHD spelling variants such as NIZAI NARAI) so rows recorded under the old combined WAZIR-S still tag as Afghan bordering.

fipv.label: fIPV Peshawar & Khyber scope (78 UCs)
fipv.portal: Peshawar & Khyber fIPV scope workbook + scope slide (Downloads)
fipv.note: Separate fIPV distribution plan for Peshawar and Khyber: 78 UCs, 1,184,376 children aged 4 months-10 years. The workbook supplies UC targets; the scope slide supplies the new/existing split and totals. Only the workbook is tracked for staleness - if the slide is revised run --only fipv --force.

icm.label: Intra-campaign monitoring (ICM) UC-wise sheet
icm.portal: EOC dashboard > Intra-campaign monitoring > export UC-wise sheet
icm.note: config.asof = null keeps the as-of date already embedded in the dashboard; set it (YYYY-MM-DD) when a new monitoring round is loaded.

pcm.label: Post-campaign monitoring (PCHS + PCM + ICM)
pcm.portal: PCHS household-check sheets + EOC post-campaign monitoring export (D:\AMAZON DATA), plus ICM columns of the KP+TD spotting workbook (reuses the chd cache)
pcm.note: One payload, three sources: the newest PCHS Data*.xlsx (campaign-wise household checks, currently Feb-Aug 2026), the newest POST CAMPAIGN MONITORING*.xlsx (currently SNID Sept-26) and per-UC ICM for the 2026 campaigns from the spotting workbook. Staleness tracks the newest matching file only - drop a new PCHS or PCM file into D:\AMAZON DATA and run --only pcm --force. When a campaign's post-campaign file arrives, it becomes the newest PCM dataset automatically. Surveyor names are never extracted (public site).

adv.label: ZD reported & covered 2024-2025 (IDIMS advance reports)
adv.portal: IDIMS > zero dose advance report > per-campaign UC export (all campaigns of a year in one file)
adv.note: Every advance_reports_*.xls under the roots is loaded - each file is self-contained, and a campaign present in several exports is taken from the newest file (so dropping a new year's file is enough). Staleness tracks only the newest file. Campaign names without a month/year go in config.campaigns; anything else unknown aborts the extract.

noc.label: NEOC intra-campaign monitoring exports (team visits, fixed sites, supervisor, transit)
noc.portal: NEOC > intra-campaign monitoring > team / fixed-site / transit / supervisor exports (CSV)
noc.note: Every icm_*.csv under Downloads is loaded; module comes from the filename (_supervisor/_fixed/_transit, plain = team visits), campaign from the Campaign name column. District names must match the dashboard spellings (ABOTABAD, BAR SWAT, ...). NEOC is login-gated - drop the CSV exports into Downloads and re-run.

novr.label: SNID campaign resource plan (district x team matrix)
novr.portal: EOC resource sheet issued with the campaign scope (D:\AMAZON DATA\SNID <campaign> folder)
novr.note: District-wise admin target + MT/SMT/CBV team matrix for the upcoming campaign, shown on the SNID Nov-26 scope tab. A new campaign resource plan csv anywhere under D:\AMAZON DATA becomes the newest source automatically; district names must match the Final Scope spellings (WAZIR-S Lower/Upper casing included).

mon.label: Monitor operations from LS 2026 Tableau workbooks (team + AIC monitoring)
mon.note: Scans every campaign folder; maps ActivityName to dashboard cq labels. Surveyor Email used for distinct counts only, never embedded. Stale duplicate folders (KP-Special-1-Jul = May byte-copy) are skipped.

icmq.label: Intra-campaign monitoring quality (team monitored + AIC visited, UC level)
icmq.portal: EOC dashboard > Intra-campaign monitoring > export UC-wise (team-monitored and AIC-visited tables)
icmq.note: One CSV per table; the "2 campaigns" exports carry the newest campaign (SNID Sept 2026) with a slightly different column set, the big exports carry the full 2021-2026 history. District x campaign aggregates are count-weighted means rounded to whole percent; -1 = indicator absent from that export. 'Total' rows are skipped. The AIC 2-campaign export has no supervisor count column, so those rows are averaged per UC (wt.aic = "uc").

surv.label: AFP surveillance: weekly updates log + line list 2023-2026 (YTD and yearly indicators, month-wise detection, pendency, case aggregates)
surv.portal: EOC surveillance cell weekly updates log + provincial AFP line list (manual download)
surv.note: Two sources per refresh: the weekly log gives YTD and 2013-2026 yearly indicator histories per district plus division roll-ups, month-wise AFP detection 2019-2026 and the newest pendency snapshot; the line list gives case aggregates only (OPV dose buckets, stool adequacy, notification/investigation timeliness, classification) - no names or addresses are extracted. The `Indicators ` sheet name has a trailing space; its district rows sit above the Grand Total and division rows below it. `refresh.py run` passes the newest file of the whole entry, which can be either source, so the extractor routes `--source` by filename (`Surv. Weekly Updates Log*` -> weekly log, `LineList-*` -> line list) and discovers the other slot itself; `--ll` overrides the line list.

afpd.label: AFP case + lab database: EOC master AFP.DBF and AFPLAB.DBF exports (2026 case, timeliness, dose-history and lab-result aggregates)
afpd.portal: EOC AFP case database + polio lab database (manual DBF export)
afpd.note: Two files per refresh: AFP.DBF is the AFP case master (one row per case, KP only, 2022-2026) and AFPLAB.DBF is the polio lab database (one row per stool specimen - cases, contacts and hotcases). Both are dBase III files with fixed-width ASCII fields; the portal writes non-standard field type codes but every value is a string and dates are YYYYMMDD. Only dates, geography, dose history and lab-result codes are read - names and addresses stay out of the payload (public GitHub Pages site). Result codes: 1 = positive, 2 = negative, 7 = pending/not done; CLASS 1 = WPV1, 2 = VDPV, 3 = discarded, blank = pending. The master databases are typically a week fresher than the published weekly log, so this payload complements SURVW rather than replacing it. Since 22-Oct-2026 the payload also carries mk (ten indicator keys) and mm (those ten per district, per year, per onset month), which is what the Surveillance tab year / month KPI filter reads; the extractor cross-checks every district-month column against dm, dy and the province y totals and aborts on any drift.

sops.label: Surveillance operations: active visits, IDIMS zero reporting, AFP pendency tracker, VPD weekly cases
sops.portal: EOC surveillance cell workbooks: active-visit tracker, IDIMS zero-report export, weekly AFP pendency tracker, VPD Sumamy weekly case counts
sops.note: Four workbooks, one payload, four separate denominators that are never blended. Active-visit (2026).xlsx gives expected/done visits per district by frequency (weekly / fortnightly / monthly) and per month; Zero Reporting IDIMS-(2026).xlsx gives site-weeks expected, received and received in time (received can exceed expected where a site reports twice); Pendency Status on -21-Oct-2026.xlsx gives the stool / case-documentation / geolocation streams as weekly snapshot blocks; Zero_Report_Cases_ONLY.xlsx (Sumamy sheet) gives weekly AFP / measles / NNT case counts. Excluded on purpose: the pendency workbook's per-record validation sheets (officer names, designations, emails, EPIDs, child names) - only the three snapshot sheets are read, and only district labels plus counts reach the payload; tracker snapshots before Mar-2023, where the older blocks carry a previous-year tally or a gap count in a rate column; the per-district weekly VPD detail (province series only, to keep the payload small). AFP counts differ by source by design - VPD weekly AFP reports, the pendency tracker line list and the AFP.DBF master are three different populations and the captions say so instead of reconciling them. IDIMS zero-report timeliness and the weekly surveillance log's own zero-report percentage use different denominators and are shown side by side, never averaged. The extractor cross-checks each workbook against its own totals and aborts on drift.

neap.label: Upcoming campaign pre-campaign readiness (NEAP district-wise status)
neap.portal: EOC dashboard > Campaign > Pre Campaign > NEAP readiness (district wise)

web.note: Login-gated (plain HTTP redirects to /login). In the signed-in portal click Export to Excel on each page (table2excel filename NEAP); _refresh/neap_auto.py picks the newest NEAP*.xls from Downloads and republishes on a schedule.

neap.note: Fourteen readiness columns per district (DPEC in time, DC/DHO, must-members, UCMO, UC secretary, AICs trained, teams trained, microplans validated, members 18+, local / govt / female member, inaccessible areas). The portal re-saves the same file under a " (n)" counter and mixes two shapes: district-wise (~35 KB) and UC-wise (Province/District/Tehsil/UC before the same 14 indicators, emitted as `u`). Whatever the newest save is, the district payload is read from the newest district-wise file and `u` from the newest UC-wise file; older-shape neapreport*/allneapreport* exports are excluded by pattern. District names must match the SND scope or the extractor aborts. The sibling ucneapreport*.xls family (a one-column UC-wise ZERO DOSE COVERED table, first seen 23-Oct-2026) matches neither NEAP*.xls nor the neapreport* exclude because fnmatch anchors the name, and it is not readiness data either - it is the covered column the zero dose pages now use for SNID Sept-26, on the owner's designation; see manual.zdcov for the route and for how it diverges from that campaign's own summary report.

mpqa.label: Micro-plan quality assessment (MPQA) scoring summary
mpqa.portal: EOC dashboard > Campaign > Pre Campaign > Micro Plan Scoring > Export to Excel
mpqa.note: Micro-plan quality assessment (MPQA) for the upcoming round. WHAT IT IS (owner, 25-Oct-2026): the assigned UC list is a targeted sample - picked at random among low-performing UCs or UCs flagged on some other indicator - and scoring every UC of a district is NOT a requirement. So the assigned share of the campaign is never a coverage target, and pass / needs improvement / serious split deliberately problem-selected plans, so they are not a province-wide micro-plan quality rate either. The one figure that is an obligation is completing the assigned list: reported / assigned. Two shapes of one round are read and reconciled: the district summary (three stacked header rows; its '#UCs Planned' and '#UCs Assessed' columns are really UCs assigned for MPQA and UCs reported, and the payload keeps them in that order) and the UC-level export (26 columns, one row per assigned UC, emitted as 'u'). Only counts are kept and every percentage is recomputed from them; the extractor aborts if a bucket fails to add back to the reported count, if reported exceeds assigned, if a recomputed value leaves the portal's printed percentage (0.006 tolerance), or if a district is outside the SND scope. The pair is cross-checked per district and on the Total row: assigned = Yes + Partial, pass = over-all >=90, needs improvement 70-89, serious = under 70 PLUS any reported row with no over-all % - that is how the portal bands a Partial row (first seen on TANK/SARANGZOONA), and it is the rule that makes the two files agree, so it is asserted rather than assumed. A same-round pair that fails to reconcile aborts; an older UC export is skipped because it describes a different assigned list. The UC export's per-item columns are read but never published: its header lists 20 checklist questions over 17 score columns, so no item label can be tied to a column with certainty - only identity, the reported state and the three headline scores survive. The file carries no campaign tag - the round label comes from the dashboard's own SND scope, the same way the NEAP payload takes it, and it is the date of the export that ties the table to this planning round. The portal re-saves the same table under a new timestamp, so one export can sit in Downloads twice (24-Oct-2026 has 02-59-57 and 03-00-11 byte-identical, md5 1f1d930f8e14c1a07ed4556791b11f39); newest mtime wins, ties broken by name. When no same-round UC file is around, 'u' is absent and the drill-down card hides itself instead of showing the summary alone. Older files in this family are a different shape - 2024-10-09 is district-wise with per-checklist-item score columns, 2024-10-14 and 2025-12-12 are UC-wise - and are refused rather than blended into this payload. The assigned denominator has been stable at 381 UCs across 27 districts since that round opened; filing moves every day (25-Oct 322 reported / 59 still to file, 26-Oct 326 / 55), so read the live counts from the payload, never from this note.

hra.label: High Risk Analysis (HRA) UC-level scoring, all districts, newest assessment per UC
hra.portal: EOC / NEOC High Risk Analysis, UC level - one workbook per division or for the whole province
hra.note: The portal's own high-risk scoring, adopted as the criteria for flagging UCs and rolling them up to districts. WHAT THE SCORE IS: 27 indicators in 4 scored blocks (geographic terrain and security access 4, epidemiology and surveillance 11, SIA operations 7, EPI-PEI synergy 5), each 0-3, plus descriptive columns with no score (drainage UC, terrain). achieved = the four block subtotals; possible = the column headed 'Total score', which is a MAXIMUM and not a score - its own formula adds a fixed 12 (geography) and 15 (EPI) to 3 x COUNT or 3 x COUNTA over the exact cells it names; band = pct > 79% Low Risk, < 60% High Risk, else Medium Risk, decided by exact integer cross-multiplication so an on-boundary row is Medium. The epi and SIA blocks hold if-applicable-else-blank indicators, so the maximum SHRINKS with the blanks and two UCs with the same failures can carry different percentages. Both the counted cell list and the counting function are read from the formula, because neither is uniform across sheets - province and most division files use COUNT over the raw columns, Mardan uses COUNTA, and Hangu divides its epi percentage by the score columns while the maximum counts the raw ones. Where the block percentages and the maximum count different lists, the band follows the maximum, because that is the column the sheet's own Risk formula divides by; such rows are counted as splitrule. The template's Rank is computed over a fixed range that does not match the rows present, so Rank is not published either. A sheet only enters the payload if its overall percentage is four-subtotals-over-its-own-maximum: HRA SW Lower.xlsx [HRA 2026] prints =maximum*100/113 with fixed block maxima, i.e. an earlier draft of the criteria card, so it is skipped and named, never blended onto a different scale. DIRECTION IS INVERTED against the dashboard's own combined UC risk score: here a HIGH percentage means LOW risk, so the two axes are never blended and HRA is always shown as Low / Medium / High with its own percentages. Columns are found by header text, never position: the same template ships with an extra Tehsil column (Abbottabad) and an extra Remarks column (Bannu), and Remarks is dropped - free text never reaches a public payload. Files merge newest-first by 8-digit UC code, so the 26-Oct-2026 Mardan Division round replaces the March province-wide rows for its UCs and the rest of the province keeps the 26-Mar-2026 vintage: there is no single as-of date and every row carries its own vintage index (vintages listed newest first in v). The Mar-2026 per-division workbooks are the same UCs as the province file, so they are superseded, not added. Asserted per row and aborting on drift: block subtotal = sum of its non-blank scores, overall pct = achieved/possible, and where the row still carries live formulas the printed maximum = what the Total-score formula's own addends compute. UC code 8 digits and unique per sheet, aggregates numeric, Risk label in the known vocabulary, district name resolvable to a dashboard spelling (ALIAS covers ABBOTTABAD, BATTAGRAM, LAKKIMARWT, LAKKI MARWAT, NORTH WAZIRISTAN). A score is blank or an integer 0-3: a text cell there (Q1, comma, 13%) is read as no score the way SUM/COUNT would, and a number outside the card excludes that row and names it (two Abbottabad rows hold 13 and 23 in a score column, which is why their own percentage prints over 100%). 1,382 of the 1,418 province rows carry their aggregates as PASTED VALUES, not formulas, so a block percentage printing over 100%, a Risk label left behind by an earlier state, a pasted maximum that no longer counts its own cells, and split-rule rows are counted in lg, printed on stdout and recomputed - never published as printed. The join to const ZD is reported and refused under 95% (97.95% on 26-Oct-2026). Read the bands from the payload, never from this note: on 26-Oct-2026 the fresh Mardan Division round assessed 132 UCs with ZERO High Risk (103 Low / 29 Medium, worst 61.1%), while the province-wide March round holds the 88 High rows of 1,418 - so a module keyed only to the portal's High band marks no district in the freshest round, which is why the focus cut is distribution-based on the dashboard side.

hrat.label: HRA UC-level compilation template (blank sheet + the divisions' own formulas)
hrat.portal: The owner's HRA UC LEVEL TEMPLATE.xlsx (D:\AMAZON DATA\HRA TEMPLATE), compiled after every campaign by divisional staff
hrat.note: The spec of the compilation sheet the dashboard reproduces online, not a dataset: column order, block merges, header wording, printed rules and number formats come from the template file, and every formula from the newest HRA workbook that still carries all 39 computed columns live and holds at least one answered cell. The template itself holds no formula by design, the Mardan Division round has its eleven epidemiology score columns pasted as values (28 of 39), and the blank card this page exports carries all 39 but no answers, so each is skipped by name and the builder aborts unless one candidate satisfies both. Named deviations, each in the payload warn list and said on the page: the NPEV rule compares a percent column with a bare 10 so the threshold is read as a percentage; the Rank range is anchored to a fixed block whatever the sheet length, so the grid ranks the rows loaded, names the count, and the download writes the range over the rows it writes (stored as _xlfn.RANK.EQ, because a bare RANK.EQ opens as #NAME?). The card's own 3*COUNT stays in the maximum: two of the three filled workbooks grade it that way, and restating it as COUNTA moves Charsadda's AGRA from 79.17% Low to 76% Medium, so a blank scores 0 as Excel does and the grid leaves an unanswered if-applicable indicator blank through ISBLANK. Pickers carry only the vocabulary the divisions type - Y/N on E and AK, Yes/No on M and BM, G1/G2/G3 plus the two compound values the province sheet writes, Green/COMVI/Red/Black, 1-4 - while F stays free text because no formula reads it and Charsadda writes Yes/No where Mardan writes Plain. Import divides a percent number by 100 in the percent columns, keeps an off-list value and names it, and names every computed cell that disagrees with the card's own formula. The downloadable workbook sets fullCalcOnLoad and writes one list validation per answered column over its exact range. Three files sit in the same family and are not this spec: HRA SW Lower.xlsx is an earlier draft of the criteria card, the per-division exports carry no live formulas, and the payload's own rows are the compiled results, not the sheet. Nothing personal is read - the sheet is geography, UC code, ratios and scores.

nact.label: SNID Nov-26 activity countdown calendar (planned timeline)
nact.portal: PEOC/NEOC countdown-of-SNIDs activity calendar issued before each round
nact.note: Manual Gantt grid: day numbers in row 2 (C..AC = Oct 5..31, AD..AS = Nov 1..16), activities 1-28 in rows 4..31, windows as cell fills (accent4 main, FF00B0F0 secondary, FFFF0000 post-campaign reviews, accent2 catch-up/LQAS days, accent6 campaign week; white + orange = grid base/Sundays). Merged notes inside the grid ride as activity notes. The B1 header supplies title/vaccine/dates; the campaign month is asserted against auto.snd.config.start so a stale calendar cannot land after the scope moves to the next round.

ind.label: Compiled campaign indicators (Admin, ICM, market survey, LQAS, PCM)
ind.portal: EOC dashboard compiled campaign indicators export (2017-2026, 85 campaigns)
ind.note: One row per UC per campaign (84 columns, 75,792 rows). The payload carries district aggregates for every campaign plus the raw UC rows of the 2025+ campaigns, so the five dashboard tables offer a district / UC toggle. Percent columns are recomputed from their count pairs; Same Day coverage and ICM Seen % have no count pair and are stored as the district mean of UC values. A literal -1 in the source counts as not reported, other negatives are kept. Keep the payload under refresh.py's 5 MB size ceiling - if the next export adds more UC-detail years, raise UC_FROM_YEAR or the ceiling.

inda.label: Admin coverage and missed children for SNID Sept 2026 (const INDA)
inda.portal: EOC summary coverage report (portal > coverage > export UC-wise): the direct export arrives as summary_<campaign>_<date>_<time>.xls with the table in the sibling <name>_files/sheet001.htm; the legacy pipeline's saved copy is cov_SNID Sept 2026.xls
inda.note: Fills the Sept-2026 gap in the compiled-indicators export: the data pack's Admin table gets SNID Sept 2026 from the same UC-wise coverage workbook as the Missed children tab. Only admin coverage/missed columns are available; MP target, same-day coverage, guest, HRMP mobile and school stay not reported, and the report's Zero Dose Covered column has no slot in INDIC's 21 admin keys (it feeds ZD and ADV instead). Keep a shell export together with its _files folder - covsept.py resolves the shell. The newest file that really carries UC rows wins, and the 23-Oct-2026 export genuinely revises the round (vaccinated 6,235,824, still missed 121,677 - unchanged from 22-Oct - while zero-dose covered rose 19,144 to 24,052; that column feeds ZD/ADV, not these 21 admin keys). The portal saves one round in two shapes under the same summary name: the UC-wise table this payload needs and a district-wise roll-up of it (province/division/district plus one measure column - the 26-Oct-2026 file is the Bannu and D.I. Khan divisions only). The roll-up is not new information and is provably a cut of the same data: its zero-dose reported column reproduces the 23-Oct UC-wise file's own district sums exactly (Bannu 4,205, Lakki Marwat 4,555, South Waziristan North 492, D.I. Khan 5,284, Tank 967, South Waziristan Lower 572, South Waziristan Upper 290 - 16,365 of the province's 62,128), so skipping it loses nothing. extract_inda.py therefore probes each candidate's header from newest mtime down, prints `SKIP inda <file>: <reason>` for every file it refuses and takes the newest one that carries UC rows - a newer wrong-shape export neither aborts the run nor gets credited as the source, because refresh.py run records the path the extractor reports reading rather than the newest match on disk. A genuine .xlsx re-save of the same round is still never a candidate: covsept.py reads header rows from HTML only, and a flattened .xlsx header aborts loudly rather than shifting figures. Drop the new export in Downloads and run --only inda.

cin.label: Campaign indicators at one plate - district and UC grain, one column per indicator (const CIN)
cin.portal: Pre-filled district/UC campaign-indicator workbook prepared by the data cell (District Wise + UC Wise tabs) from the portal's compiled campaign export
cin.note: Stores only SNID Sept 2026. The workbook's Feb/Apr/May 2026 blocks are a re-cut of the data the dashboard already carries - the extractor proves them equal to INDIC row for row at both grains (district: target, still NA, SM %, ICM recall %, LQAS pass %; UC rows on Administrative Target 1418/1418, 1417/1418 and 928/928) and proves the Sept district admin block equal to INDA on six columns, 17,415 values in all - so only the fourth round is emitted. Earlier rounds merge from INDIC into the same 17 columns at render time: one copy of the data, so the plate and the data pack cannot disagree. Tab shapes differ and are asserted: the district tab has no ICM Total Missed, the UC tab no ICM TVBCM, so a row keeps -1 where its tab stops and the page leaves a column out only when no campaign in the selection reports it (the caption names it). Units are declared and proved: Feb/Apr/May percentages are fractions on both tabs; Sept district is already percent, Sept UC SM% is percent while ICM%/LQAS% are fractions. 975 UC rows are counted and skipped from the cross-check because the workbook groups by district+UC name while the portal keeps the tehsil split (Bannu's two AMANDI UCs sum into one workbook row); six Lakki Marwat UCs absent from the Sept summary report keep the workbook's row with only their admin columns uncross-checked. Sept covers 37 districts - the coverage report has no old Wazir-S district, only Lower and Upper. Drop the new workbook in Downloads and run --only cin.

epm.label: EPI month index (EMETA) with the 2023-2026 monthly exports
epm.note:
Every single-month export's own period header (
YYYY-MM - YYYY-MM
) is read; per-district aggregates are cached in _refresh/cache/epi25mon.pkl keyed by file id, so only new files pay the pandas parse. Months already embedded in index.html are kept unless their own export is on disk, in which case the parsed month replaces them. A month carrying a part-report flag from an earlier build loses it (and its reporting % and the `partial` captions go with it) once its own single-month export is on disk - Sep 2026 did on 28-Oct-2026, when its export re-added to the YTD register. Run together with epim. The dose panel the EPI section reads (EMETA.ag) is regenerated from the shared spec _refresh/epi_ag.py; cached months carry that panel as an agv signature, so entries parsed under an older panel are skipped rather than trusted.

epim.label: EPI district-month coverage rows (EPIM) with 2023-2026
epim.note: Companion to epm (same parse cache). Every month with an export on disk is rebuilt from it, 2026 included since 28-Oct-2026 (the embedded 2026 rows had been frozen at eleven core doses with a part-report September); a month with no on-disk export keeps the embedded rows rather than vanishing from the year. An EPI district not in the embedded mapping aborts the extract. Every rebuilt month carries the full 19-dose epi_ag panel.

epiuc.label: EPI UC-month dose counts (EPIUC): Jan-Dec 2023, Jan-Dec 2025 and Jan-Sep 2026
epiuc.note: Companion to epim (same discovery and parse cache): one row per UC per month for every UC-wise month - Jan-Dec 2023, Jan-Dec 2025 and Jan-Sep 2026 (33 months) - rebuilt from those monthly exports. 2024 is district-level, so it yields no UC-month rows; the 2026 months arrived 28-Oct-2026 and their per-UC sums reproduce the embedded EPI YTD register exactly. Values are dose counts, never percentages; rows stay aligned to the embedded EPI order and the extractor aborts if the UC count or the embedded mapping changes, and every district-month must re-add to EPIM. When a month is on disk twice, the newest UC-wise copy wins (older district-level copies disagree: Jan 2025 bcg 2,538 over its UCs vs 2,119 in a summary). A month EMETA flags as a part-report is not published at UC grain.

rca.label: EPI-MIS rapid coverage assessments, visit-level (const ERCA)
rca.note: Every RCA_Report*.xls is loaded (each export covers its own date range); month x district aggregates are cached per file id (_refresh/cache/rcamon.pkl). Newest file wins per month x district. Monitor names/IDs/designations are never extracted (public site). RCA_Report (36).xls (16-Oct-2026) is a NATIONAL export (GB/Punjab/Sindh/ICT districts, 593 rows) that is not the KP series - excluded in sources.json.

esup.label: EPI supervisory checklist visits, fixed + outreach (const ESUP)
esup.note: Every Supervisory_Checklist_Report*.xls is loaded (2026 arrives as two exports: fixed-site and outreach). Newest file wins per month x district x site type; per-file cache in _refresh/cache/esumon.pkl. Monitor names/CNICs/designations are never extracted (public site).

ptp.label: Permanent Transit Points coverage panel (const PTP)
ptp.portal: IDIMS > PTP Panel (idims.eoc.gov.pk/ptpPanel.php?comp_id=2) > PTP Coverage export
ptp.note: The export is tab-separated text with an .xls name, one row per post per reporting day. Aggregated to district x year, district x month and UC x year/month. Downloads is scanned first because the portal exports land there and srcutil picks the newest file across both roots. Posts are keyed on Site_ID, falling back to ID: from the 23-Oct-2026 export ID is a per-row id (263,024 rows, 263,024 IDs) and the post number moved to Site_ID (1,150), while older exports have no Site_ID and their ID is that same post number - Site_IDs 805 and 782 are the 20-Apr-2025 export's IDs 805 and 782, same UC codes, same post names. District spellings are matched case-insensitively where unambiguous: the same export writes WAZIR-S LOWER / WAZIR-S UPPER where the 2025 export wrote WAZIR-S Lower, and an exact match silently drops the 20,539 rows behind those two spellings. no_of_refusals is summed but is non-zero only from 2026; the payload publishes that boundary as reft so the UI shows a dash, not a false zero, for earlier years. PostName and PostLocation are never extracted - they name fixed checkpoints and this is a public site. Coverage, Coverage_under5/above5, OPVGiven/Used/Returned, VacRecvd and aav_cards are held out of the payload: in the 24-Oct-2026 export Coverage totals 53.4M against ExpChildrenDay 34.0M and exceeds it in 143,830 rows, the under5/above5 split is populated in only 3,997 rows (none before 2023), and the Coverage/Exp median drifts from 3.71 in 2016 to 0.66 in 2026, so the field is not one thing over time; OPVGiven reconciles to Used+Returned to within 0.005%, i.e. it is vaccine issued to the post, not doses administered. Nothing built on those columns is published until the report definition is confirmed. Row detail also carries no surveyor fields, unlike the nine *_combined_*.csv checklist exports in the same folder, which do (surveyor_name, designation, Surveyor Email, teams_valid_cnic, per-row latitude/longitude).

ptpm.label: PTP field monitoring: HRMP checklist, spot-survey and logistics exports (const PTPM)
ptpm.note: Three HRMP checklist exports in the Raw IDIMS folder, one payload: PTPs-STPs_Monitoring_Checklist-176 (one row per monitoring visit), PTPs-STPs_Spot_Survey_Checklist-52 (one row per spot survey) and PTPs-STPs_Logistic_Check_List-51 (one row per logistics check). Aggregated to district x year and district x month on the same district index and the same month-slot arithmetic as const PTP, so the PTP tab can drive both grids from one period picker. Posts join on ptp_loc = the coverage panel's Site_ID (250 of 258 monitored, 450 of 460 surveyed, 358 of 365 logistics-checked posts are on the Oct-2026 panel; the remainder are counted as off-panel, not dropped). The field data stops where these exports stop (21-Apr-2025) and the reporting panel runs to Oct-2026, so no monitoring period overlaps the current reporting period and the block says so instead of drawing an empty 2026. Monitoring months come from date_conducted; the spot and logistics exports have no conduct date, so their months are entry months. Published: checklist/survey/logistics counts, distinct posts reached, teams present and teams monitored. Held out: every name, email, designation, CNIC-derived field, free-text remarks and the per-row latitude/longitude (public site); the integer answer codes shift, docs_avail, app_loc, post_identity, team_identity, security_pres, sup_visit, secu_assist1, site_type and incoming_type, which no caption in the export or in the three .twbx workbooks beside them decodes; teams_trained, teams_adult, teams_local, teams_zero_dose, teams_local_lang, carr_tall_avail, vial_maint and vacc_match, which agree with teams_monitored in 99.2-99.8% of rows because the form mirrors one answer across them; total_team and transit_teams, sane in 15,094 rows but 202 teams at a post where 2 were present and 141 where 1 was in the rest; the up_to_10/above_10/*_fm/nofm family (233 of 20,219 rows, all site_type 9) alongside the up_to_5/nofm_5 family (19,986 rows, all site_type 1) - two survey designs in one table that must not be blended; and the 15 logistics item families (ilr, ilrn, ref, cab, bann, jack, pcap, id, paper, stand, cooler, vcarr, humber, chair, other x total/available/workable/nrepair/nreplace), whose abbreviations are undefined and whose available exceeds total in 846 family rows. The extractor aborts unless each source's month cells add back to its year cells and to its kept-row count, no month cell exceeds its year cell on any column, every read row is either kept or dropped under a named reason, and no post is monitored under two districts.
ptpm.portal: IDIMS > HRMP field monitoring exports (raw folder, not re-pulled since 21-Apr-2025)

mtm.label: HRMP mobile and migrant teams: the six unmapped IDIMS forms (const MTM)
mtm.note: Six HRMP mobile-team exports in the same Raw IDIMS folder as the three PTP field-check forms, pulled together on 21-Apr-2025 and never re-pulled: Migrant_and_Mobile_Populations_Mapping_Form-174 (one row per mapping record), Nomads_immunization_team_activity_-130 and Search_Team_Activity-157 and Special_Biker_Teams__Coverage-178 (one row per team activity or coverage report) and Monitoring_checklist_Nomads_immunization_team_-137 and Search_Team_Monitoring_Checklist-158 (one row per monitoring checklist). Aggregated to district x year and district x month on the same district index, year list and month-slot arithmetic as const PTP and const PTPM, so the PTP tab drives all three grids from one period picker. One spelling in the mapping form is not on the KP district index (KOLAIPALAS, 2 rows) and is dropped under a named reason rather than guessed onto a district. Every month is the month the entry was made: only three of the six carry a separate activity date, and those disagree with the entry month in 12.8% of search-team and 8% of biker rows. Team numbers repeat across districts - the nomad form holds 23 distinct numbers province-wide but 63 once scoped to their district, the biker form 29 against 82 - so team counts are district-scoped unions and the province figure is the sum of those; the export carries no province-wide team id. Published: rows filed, as one column per form rather than one shared total so a period view can say which form filed them, mapping records by household origin (origin_country 1 is Pakistan-origin and 2 Afghan-origin, proven by orgin_dist_pak being blank in 31,694 of 31,694 Afghan-origin rows and filled in 83,206 of 83,207 Pakistan-origin ones), sessions planned against sessions conducted, children missed as not available or as a refusal, under-two zero-dose recorded, EPI cards issued, biker refusals and not-availables recorded against still open, and AFP and AEFI tallies. Held out: every name, email, user id, designation, coordinate, free-text remark and settlement or area name (public site); every target_*, coverage_* and un_recorded_*_coverage column, which is the same field family the PTP panel holds out under the open IDIMS report-definition question - in these exports they are child counts rather than percentages, but coverage exceeds target in 4,245 of 103,143 search rows and one target_ipv_1 is -3, so nothing is published on them until the definition is confirmed; the bare dose columns, empty in every live search-team row and sitting in the nomad form beside three mutually inconsistent OPV tallies (vacc_opv 203,129 against opv_does1+2+3 192,307 against target_opv 245,337); no_of_families and no_of_child, whose median is 3 but where 906 rows carry more than 100 children, up to 7,640 in one mapping record, a tail holding 20% of the province sum; mmp_types, hrmp_type, riadmin, duration (max 100,000,000), mob_pop_card_issued (max 3,134 in one session), team_planned (0, 1 and 8) and every checklist item column, all integer answer codes with no caption - and in the two monitoring checklists items_checked, data_Recording, vaccination and search_team are blank in every row. The extractor aborts unless each form's month cells add back to its year cells and to its kept-row count, no cell exceeds its year cell on any column, every read row is kept or dropped under a named reason, the origin split adds back to the mapping rows, the province sessions-conducted total does not exceed sessions-planned, the biker still-open tallies do not exceed their recorded columns, and the emitted cell arrays contain nothing but numbers. A negative in a published count column voids that one cell and is counted rather than fatal or silently added: one search-team row at Peshawar writes session_conducted -2, the visit happened so the row and its other columns stand, and the column is the sum of the usable values.
mtm.portal: IDIMS > HRMP mobile and migrant team exports (raw folder, not re-pulled since 21-Apr-2025)

sta.label: HRMP search teams: the two forms as the owner pulled them (const STA)
sta.portal: IDIMS > Search Team Activity Peshawar and Search Team Monitoring Check LIst, saved by the owner as Tableau workbooks (both re-pulled 26-Oct-2026; extract_sta.py takes the pull date from the two workbook file mtimes, never a constant, so a newer row is never reported as activity filed after the pull) - no script fetches IDIMS and no credentials are read
sta.note: The same two IDIMS search-team forms `auto.mtm` publishes from the 21-Apr-2025 CSV exports, read later and deeper out of the owner's own Tableau workbooks: `Search Team Activity Peshawar.twbx` (one row per activity report) and `Search Team Monitoring Check LIst.twbx` (one row per monitoring checklist, in the filename's own capitalisation). Vintage is proved rather than assumed and the proof travels in `vint`: of the 15,282 row ids in the April activity CSV, 15,281 also sit in the workbook and the 1 that does not is carried into these totals under its own id (`n.sact.carried`) instead of being lost, while the workbook adds 11,978 rows filed since April; checklists share 6,001 of 6,001 ids, none missing, and add 5,009 newer rows. Two vintages of two forms, not two more forms, so nothing on this card is ever added to the mobile-team card above it and the caption says so. 27,279 activity rows read -> 26,698 kept (562 archived under the source's own `is_archive` flag, 20 repeated `unique_id`) plus the 1 carried id; 11,011 checklist rows read -> 11,001 kept (9 archived, 1 repeated id). Aggregated to district x year and district x month on the same district index, year list and month-slot arithmetic as `PTP`, `PTPM` and `MTM`, so the PTP tab's single Year -> month picker scopes all four grids; panel window 2016-2026, both forms spanning 2023-09..2026-10 with no month hole in either (`gap` empty), so a dash anywhere is a district that did not file and never a source gap. What the owner pointed at is here and it is not what the column names suggest: the activity form carries a dose column for every antigen in the ladder and every one of them is blank in all 27,279 workbook rows. What the form actually holds is a target and a coverage figure per antigen, so the measure published is that pair - 21 pairs (zero-dose, new-born, BCG, OPV 0-3, Penta 1-3, Pneumo 1-3, Rota 1-2, IPV 1-2, IPV booster, TD) as children targeted, children covered, and the rows that wrote a pair contradicting themselves, each pair keeping its own void count instead of those rows being quietly dropped: 600 zero-dose, 1,378 OPV-3 and 593 BCG voided rows. The ladder is district x year only, never by month: a target for a month the team did not work is exactly what the void rule exists to catch. `td` is withheld outright by a computed rule - a pair is refused when more than a fifth of the rows that recorded it contradicted themselves, and td sits at 33.6% (8,959 of the 26,696 that recorded it) where the worst column that is published manages 7.7%: the form fills td's coverage side and almost never its target side, so across the whole pull 18,938 covered were written against a target of 3 and, once the row rule has voided the contradictions, the pair would publish as 3 targeted against nothing covered. It renders as a labelled `Withheld` row carrying those four numbers, not as a silent absence. That is also the answer the transit-point panel still holds open (#156): for these two forms the owner's workbook settles that the target/coverage family means targeted / covered / self-contradicting, so the pairs are published here while the PTP export's own `Coverage` columns stay held out - a divergence between two sources of one field family, named on both cards rather than resolved by picking the prettier number. Every published month is the month the entry was made: activity month and entry month differ in 4,150 rows, 1 row's activity date cannot be read at all, sessions conducted exceed sessions planned in 156, 4 `ipv_booster` cells are not numbers, and covered-above-target runs per antigen (largest ipv_1 at 2,065) - all of it in `n.sact.dq` and said in the caption, while the checklist form disagrees with itself nowhere (`n.smon.dq` empty). The checklist's 32 item columns split into 25 answered by at least one row, published per district, and 7 no row ever answered (search_team, logistics, vaccination, cold_chain, team_assistant, data_recording, operational_modality); the last group is named in `inever` and never rendered as a 0. Team and UC counts are district-scoped unions summed (activity 56 team numbers and 96 UCs across districts against 24 and 95 distinct province-wide; checklist 55/93 against 26/92) because a team number repeats across districts and the export carries no province-wide team id. District spellings match the KP index case-insensitively where unambiguous - `WAZIR-S LOWER` on this form is the panel's SW Wazir Belt - and a spelling that matches two districts aborts the build instead of picking one; 8 district units carry search-team rows (Bannu, D.I. Khan, Lakki Marwat, Malakand, Peshawar, SW Mehsud Belt, SW Wazir Belt, Shangla) and activity reports sit in 5 of them. `tri` sets the two registers side by side over the 33 months both cover (2024-01 to 2026-09, from `const EPIM`, the facility EPI register): facility OPV-3 and BCG doses against the search team's covered sides plus the report count behind them, with the ratio published as search-team OPV-3 per 100 facility doses - two registers of the same districts, never a coverage percentage, and a search-team figure above 100 per 100 aborts the build rather than being published. `lnk` is the team-number linkage per district: 236 activity team-months, 271 checklist team-months, 166 on both forms, kept as counts because a district with 147 activity team-months and 121 matched is a different finding from one with a single checklist month and no activity at all, and one percentage would flatten both. Held out of the payload and named in the caption (`hold`, 9 groups): the reporter names, the address they sign with, the entry and update ids and the vaccinator/monitor/focal-person columns; position coordinates and their accuracy; every free-text note including why a row was archived; the reporting body and post columns; the bare dose columns blank in all 27,279 rows; `un_recorded_<antigen>_coverage` (a third number that reconciles with the pair in none of the rows checked); the ladder by month; `td`; the 7 never-answered checklist fields. No name, address, coordinate or remark reaches this file - the site is public. The extractor aborts unless the district x year and district x month cells add back to the kept-row count in every published column, no month cell exceeds its year cell, every read row is kept or dropped under a named reason, each antigen pair's three counts tie to the rows that recorded it, the ladder ties back to the pair counts, the item columns tie to `iyes` + `inever`, the linkage sums tie to `n.link`, and no district spelling is ambiguous. **Route - `refresh.py run --only sta` since 27-Oct-2026.** `python _refresh/extract_sta.py` writes `_refresh/out/sta.json`; it accepts `--source` and ignores it, because both workbooks are named in full and the pull date comes from their own file mtimes. `python _refresh/patch_sta_ui.py` owns the card (`const STA` after `const MTM`, the `cSTa` card between the mobile-team card and the district inventory, `staTab()`, the render block, six CSV buttons and the four corrections this makes to the `MTM` caption and its hint) and reverses all of it byte for byte with `--unpatch`. `const STA` is in every variant since the 26-Oct-2026 14:43 sync and `state.json` has both a `sta` and an `mtm` ledger entry, so `run` re-extracts and swaps the payload into all four variants in one step; `refresh.py` records the apply, so a later run skips the dataset as unchanged and a `--force` re-extract that changes nothing is reported byte-identical instead of rewriting the files.

zd.label: ZD Digitization (IDIMS comparison report)
zd.portal: IDIMS / SMC Tracker > Comparison Report export
zd.howto: Drop the newest Comparison_Report_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx into BOTH D:\AMAZON DATA and C:\Users\HD\Downloads (the legacy pipeline scans Downloads), then rebuild and harvest - see SOURCES.md, 'Harvesting from the legacy pipeline'. DATA needs two reports: the newest one plus the latest one from a DIFFERENT campaign, which supplies the rp/lp comparison columns. Never run zd_refresh.py against this repo - it rebuilds from dashboard_template.html and would drop every tab added after 10-Oct-2026.

zdcov.label: ZD Reported & Covered (multi-campaign coverage workbook)
zdcov.portal: IDIMS > zero dose reported/covered export, one per campaign, saved as _portal\cov_<campaign>.xls in the legacy folder
zdcov.howto: Update D:\AMAZON DATA\ZERO DOSE REPORTED AND COVERED.xlsx and/or drop new cov_<campaign>.xls overlays into C:\Users\HD\Downloads\ZD_Dashboard\_portal, then rebuild and harvest (see SOURCES.md). ZD is NOT produced by the Comparison Report - do not confuse it with the zd entry above. Coverage-only refresh (adds a campaign's covered/pct/band to the UC table): run `python _refresh/extract_zdcov.py`, then `python _refresh/refresh.py inject --const ZD --from _refresh/out/zd.json`. It reads the same UC-wise coverage reports as the mism dataset (manual.mism.scans, newest export per campaign) and only touches the slot named S in `slots`, after proving that report's reported-ZD and household-target columns against const ZD row by row. April and May keep whatever the workbook already carried. Current source (23-Oct-2026, designated by the owner): C:\Users\HD\Downloads\ucneapreport261023053947.xls - the portal's UC-wise one-column ZERO DOSE COVERED table, taken as SNID Sept-26's coverage measured against the recorded SNID Sept-26 reported counts. Route: `python _refresh/extract_zdcov.py --uc-covered <that file> --out _refresh/out/zd_uc.json`, then `python _refresh/refresh.py inject --const ZD --from _refresh/out/zd_uc.json`, then `python _refresh/refresh.py run --only adv --force` because ADV joins const ZD, before anything that reads adv.json. The extractor joins by UC code and aborts on a duplicate code, an export row that is not a tracked UC, or a Total row that disagrees with the sum of its own rows; April and May keep whatever the workbook already carried. What it gives: 1,402 UC rows, 39,176 covered against 62,128 reported (63.1%), 93 UCs explicitly 0, 323 UCs above their own recorded count (286 of them over 110%, which the campaign tab bands as Verify rather than a pass), 15 tracked UCs with no Sept record at all. It replaces the campaign's own summary coverage report of the same date (C:\Users\HD\Downloads\summary_SNID Sept 2026_2026-10-23_052653.xls - 24,052 covered on the same 62,128 reported; the 22-Oct export gave 19,144). The two disagree UC by UC on 872 of the 975 UCs where the summary reports a figure, and this column reproduces SNID May-26's per-UC covered on 836 of 921 UCs (its May-scope subtotal is May's 26,620 exactly), so on the evidence it reads as a carried-forward register rather than a Sept-only count - which is why both figures are named, and the divergence stated, wherever the covered column leads: the ZD page hint, the comparison caveats, the all-UC table caption, the coverage chart caption, the Summary KPI subtitle and insight, the advance-report page hint and source caption, and the gap-closure caption.

val.label: ZD Validation (child-level app export)
val.portal: SMC Tracker form 200 > combined export (login required)
val.howto: Save the combined CSV export as C:\Users\HD\Downloads\ZD_Dashboard\_portal\val_<campaign>.csv (move the previous copy into _portal\_prev). Each val_*.csv REPLACES every master row of the campaigns it contains, so keep one file per campaign. Then rebuild and harvest (see SOURCES.md). VCH is the only payload that differs per variant: the internal build carries nm/fn plus real cd/mo, the public build drops nm and fn and blanks cd and mo. Derive the public one from the internal one - never copy either way blindly. Do NOT mirror these CSVs into the repo's own _portal folder: it is published on GitHub Pages and they carry child names, father names, EPI card numbers, monitor names and surveyor emails.

epi.label: Routine EPI coverage (UC YTD + district monthly)
epi.howto: EMETA/EPIM refresh automatically (auto.epm + auto.epim) from the single-month exports and are never derived from a year-to-date file. The UC-level payload is rebuilt from the UC-wise export opened for the year-to-date period (Report Type = all_ucs): python _refresh/extract_epi_ytd.py --source "<file>.xls" --out _refresh/out/epi_ytd.json, then python _refresh/refresh.py inject --const EPI --from _refresh/out/epi_ytd.json and --const EPIYTD --from _refresh/out/epi_ytd.meta.json. The extractor refuses any UC code, name or district that differs from what is embedded, so the reviewed polio UC matching can never be silently re-made; rows with no district are dropped only when every value in them is zero. Rows carry the 19-dose panel from _refresh/epi_ag.py (the eleven flagged core are what the tables show; the UC CSV holds all 19): a dose the export does not carry is stored as missing and never defaults to last period's number or to 0%.

epidrop.label: Routine dropout report (district level)
epidrop.howto: python _refresh/extract_epi_drop.py --source "<file>.xls" --out _refresh/out/epi_drop.json, then inject --const EPIDROP. Published dropout % per district for five dose pairs; the province Total row is kept as the report's own all-KP figure and is never averaged across districts. Reported rates differ from the dashboard's coverage-derived dropout columns (different arithmetic, sex-split cohorts) - both are shown side by side on the EPI coverage page.

mpqah.label: Micro-plan quality assessment, every campaign round
mpqah.portal: EOC dashboard > Campaign > Pre Campaign > MPQA (NEW) for Sept-2026 onward, MPQA (OLD) for May-2026 and earlier
mpqah.howto: Harvest once per batch from the signed-in portal (POST form.searchform: compaignid[] per round, province[] KP, blank district[] for all, dataview 3 for the UC table and 2 for the district summary) into _refresh/cache/mpqa_hist_<date>.json as {asof,harvested,src,rounds:{<round>:{d,u}}}, then python _refresh/extract_mpqa_hist.py (reads the newest cache file) and refresh.py inject --const MPQAH --from _refresh/out/mpqah.json. One payload per campaign round - the 29-Oct-2026 harvest carries 11, NID FEB 2025 to SNID Nov 2026. Counts only, and only the nine identity/score columns both portal formats carry, because the item columns differ (17 in the NEW UC export, 21 in the OLD one) and no item label can be tied to a column with certainty. The extractor asserts per district that planned = UC rows, assessed = Yes + Partial, the three buckets = the portal's own district summary, UC codes unique and district sets equal, and reproduces const MPQA row for row for Nov-26. A cache rebuild, not a Downloads pickup: refresh.py run cannot find it, so a harvest ends with the extractor and inject by hand. Read by the Campaign indicators plate (one round per campaign row); const MPQA stays the single Nov-26 round the Pre-campaign card, the home trigger popover and extract_trig.py read.

kpgeo.label: KP district map geometry (const KPGEO)
roots: D:\extra tasks\KP UC Shapefile\KP UC Shapefile
kpgeo.portal: no portal - boundary shapefiles on disk (district geometry + the 23-Oct-2021 UC layer)
kpgeo.howto: One-off build; re-run only if the boundary files are replaced. python _refresh/extract_kpgeo.py prints the labelling vote, --emit writes _refresh/out/kpgeo.json, then python _refresh/refresh.py inject --const KPGEO --from _refresh/out/kpgeo.json. The district file ships geometry with no .dbf, so its 37 polygons are named by a containment vote of the PK_Admin4-KP_UCs layer whose Ucode joins to the dashboard's own EPI UC rows (1,152 of 1,414 resolve): majority district per polygon, at least 5 dashboard-resolved UCs and 75% agreement, and the build aborts unless every one of the 37 dashboard districts is claimed exactly once (it does - including BAR SWAT vs SWAT and WAZIR-S Upper vs Lower, which the boundary file itself cannot tell apart). Rings are Douglas-Peucker simplified at 0.0025 deg with max-deviation and area-drift asserts, so a collapsed district fails the build. Geometry only - no people, no UC detail.

cq.label: Campaign quality / intra-campaign operational indicators
cq.howto: Export from NEOC into _portal/camp_quality.json, or use the in-dashboard NEOC import block on the Intra-campaign tab (stores to localStorage, never to the repo).

mism.label: Missed children & refusals
mism.portal: EOC dashboard > per-campaign coverage export (login required), UC-wise Summary report
mism.howto: Run `python _refresh/extract_mis.py`, then inject both payloads: `python _refresh/refresh.py inject --const MIS --from _refresh/out/mis.json` and `--const MISM --from _refresh/out/mism.json` (MIS/MISM stay separate payloads, so refresh.py run cannot drive them). For each tracked campaign the newest readable export wins: the saved _portal\cov_<campaign>.xls copies and the direct summary_<campaign>_<date>_<time>.xls exports (keep its _files folder alongside) hold identical figures for Apr-26 and May-26, so a fresh Sept round export simply revises that campaign. Add a new round to `campaigns` and to the Downloads patterns when it is reported; the extractor aborts if a tracked campaign has no readable report. Not derived from the val_*.csv validation exports - those feed the val entry. Current sources (23-Oct-2026): Apr-26 and May-26 still from the newest Downloads exports, Sept-26 from C:\Users\HD\Downloads\summary_SNID Sept 2026_2026-10-23_052653.xls - 3,719 rows in total (Sept 1,402, May 928, Apr 1,389); the Sept re-export left every MIS value unchanged (vaccinated 6,235,824, still missed 121,677) and only moved the zero-dose covered column, which ZD owns.

surv.label: Surveillance (AFP + district surveillance)
surv.howto: Refresh the _portal JSON exports, then rebuild SURVM/AFP.

neoc.label: NEOC operational indicators (AIC visited, teams monitored)
neoc.howto: In-dashboard import only: Intra-campaign tab > NEOC block > paste table / import CSV-TSV-HTML export / run the copied snippet in your own NEOC console. Stored in localStorage['kpNEOC.icm.v1'], never committed. Session cookies are not used by any script here.

trig.label: EOC control-room triggers (MPQA, ICM, admin coverage) - district-wise
trig.portal: EOC dashboard > Control Room Triggers (https://www.eoc.gov.pk/trigger/index), signed-in browser
trig.howto: Read the three trigger tables while signed in to the EOC portal with campaign NOV-26-1 and province 3:KP; the portal prints zeros until the round starts, so ICM and admin coverage stay on SEP-26-1. Save the scraped tables to _refresh/cache/trig_<date>.json as {src,asof,note,tables:{mpqa,icm,admin}}, each with per-district [flagA,flagB,total,feedback] plus tot. Then run python _refresh/extract_trig.py (checks a+b==total, feedback<=total, the Total row against the column sums, duplicate districts, and matches the MPQA trigger table against the embedded MPQA payload) and inject with refresh.py inject --const TRIG --from _refresh/out/trig.json. Counts are UCs only - no child names, no feedback text, no credentials read or stored.
